name: remote-desktop
description: A Linux desktop streamed into a tab as low-latency video (H.265 or H.264 from the GPU) with full keyboard, mouse, clipboard, cursor and audio (on its own virtual desktop, which follows the tab's size and scale), or attached to an existing desktop (X11, wlroots, GNOME or KDE, with its sound and clipboard). Powered by remote-pc: its host, rpc-host, downloads from the project's releases with one click.

enumItemLabels: Managed display (virtual desktop that follows the tab)
remoteDesktop.mode.description: Managed: start a virtual display (headless sway) with a desktop session on it, and let the desktop follow the tab's size and scale. Existing: attach to the desktop already running on this machine (an X11 desktop, or a wlroots compositor such as sway); input goes to that real screen and its size is never changed. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.display.description: Existing mode only: the desktop to attach to: an X display, e.g. ":0", a wlroots compositor's socket, e.g. "wayland-1", "gnome" or "kde". Leave empty to detect the running desktop.

remoteDesktop.desktopCommand.description: Managed mode only: the command that starts the desktop environment (e.g. xfce4-session, startlxde, mate-session), run on a rootful Xwayland inside the virtual display. Must be installed on the host.

remoteDesktop.useGlobalConfig.description: Managed mode only: run the desktop with your own config directory (~/.config) instead of a fresh one each Start, so your theme, panel and window manager settings apply and changes made on the virtual desktop are kept. If the same desktop also runs on this machine's screen at the same time, both sessions share those files. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.keyboardLayout.description: XKB layout for the virtual display (managed mode; also the keyboard added to an existing Wayland desktop), e.g. us, de, fr. Keys are forwarded by physical position, so this should match the keyboard you type on. Text from phone keyboards is typed as characters whatever the layout.

remoteDesktop.port.description: Preferred loopback port for the stream. If it is taken, the next free port is used.

remoteDesktop.bitrateKbps.description: Upper bitrate limit in kilobits per second. The stream adapts below it when the connection struggles, and the viewer's quality preset caps it further. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.codec.description: Video codec for the stream. Every tab and device viewing the desktop shares the codec (viewers who don't drive get a separate, smaller stream in the same codec), so Auto keeps it on H.264; H.265 looks sharper at the same bitrate, but each viewing browser must decode it (one that can't shows "No common codec"). Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.pixelRatio.description: Default remote pixels per CSS pixel for your devices. Auto detects each device's pixel ratio (capped at 2, so a 3x phone gets a 2x desktop). Each browser can override this for itself from the viewer tab's view settings; the desktop follows the ratio of the tab that drives it.

remoteDesktop.serverPath.description: Path to your own rpc-host build. Leave empty to use the rpc-host downloaded from the Remote Desktop panel (or one on PATH or in ~/.cargo/bin). Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.udpPort.description: The UDP port native remote-pc clients (rpc-client) on other machines connect to; the panel shows it with a PIN for pairing. Open it in the firewall. 0 keeps the desktop on this machine (browser tabs don't need the port). Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.followerFps.description: frame rate of the stream sent to viewers who watch while someone else drives (1–30). Their stream is a separate, smaller one, so the driver keeps most of the bandwidth; fewer frames take less still. Takes effect on the next Start.

enumItemLabels: Auto (the GPU when it opens, else software)
remoteDesktop.renderer.description: Managed mode only: how the virtual desktop renders. Software (pixman) needs no GPU; without a GPU encoder rpc-host also encodes on the CPU (H.264 with OpenH264, up to 3840x2160 at 30 fps, fewer frames on a slow CPU), whatever this says. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.portMapping.description: Ask the router to forward the UDP port (PCP, NAT-PMP or UPnP) so native remote-pc clients outside this network connect directly, over IPv4 or IPv6. The panel shows whether it worked. Browser tabs don't need it. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.rendezvous.description: A remote-pc rendezvous server (NAME#KEY, from its `rpc-rendezvous key`), for native clients outside this network when the router can't forward the port (carrier NAT, UPnP off): it introduces them, punches a direct path, or relays. Clients learn it from this desktop during any session. Empty: none. Needs a UDP port above. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.relayUrl.description: The rendezvous server's WebSocket relay (wss://NAME/rpc-relay), for native clients on networks that block UDP. Empty: none. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.followerSize.description: The size of the stream viewers watch while someone else drives (that many lines' worth of pixels, the desktop's shape kept). Larger is sharper but costs the host more encoding and every follower more bandwidth; full size on a 5K desktop roughly doubles the encoding work. Takes effect on the next Start.
